title: SAFEAIR: Secure Airway Prediction through Flexible Endoscopy and Artificial Intelligence Recognition
summary:
During the induction of anesthesia, a breathing tube is inserted through the mouth into the trachea (“intubation”) to enable artificial ventilation for the duration of the operation. In a few patients, however, this intubation is difficult or even impossible due to various factors. This can quickly lead to a life-threatening condition if the oxygen supply cannot be ensured. All patients are therefore examined externally by an anesthetist during the preliminary anesthesia consultation for signs of obstacles or difficulties during intubation. This examination is important but cannot rule out problems with absolute certainty. That's why we're looking for additional ways to offer our patients the greatest possible safety. In the ENT clinic, all patients are examined again by an ENT doctor before an operation. This person looks through the nose with an endoscope, i.e. a small camera at the end of a thin, flexible tube, and can also look at the larynx and examine it. This can provide additional information that can indicate difficulties during intubation. 
We would like to use the images from the endoscope to obtain additional information for intubation. To do this, we put the video files into a computer network that is able to analyze them independently (“machine learning” / “artificial intelligence”) and make a statement about upcoming problems. With each video, the network learns to better assess the airway and should ultimately be able to make a prediction very reliably. This allows the anesthesia procedure to be changed and a strategy for intubation (insertion of the ventilation tube into the trachea) that is safe for the patient to be chosen without an unforeseen, dangerous situation occurring.

interventions.name: Patients who get a transnasal endoscopy which undergo HNT-surgery and get intubated

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Surgery at HNT-Department with endotracheal intubation
Exclusion criteria:
Minor patients
Patients undergoing emergency surgery
Patients with known intubation difficulties who need to be intubated while awake
Patients who do not require intubation due to surgery
